## Goal
`tests/codex/test_cx_dev_source_citations.py:16-21` checks a fixed list of four docs, so `docs/dev/CONTRIBUTING_BROKERS.md`, `DEPENDENCIES.md`, `STRINGS_CLI.md` and every new guide go unchecked.

## Order
Start last among the docs WOs, after WO-230, WO-231, WO-232, WO-250, WO-252 and WO-253 are merged, so the glob covers their files. No other open WO edits this file.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. Replace the fixed `DOCS` tuple with a sorted glob of `docs/dev/*.md` and `docs/i18n/*.md`, parametrised with the file name as the test id, so a new doc is covered without editing the test.
2. Keep the existing parsing rules and the documented limitation (lines 1-5).
3. A failure names the doc, the citation and the reason; an opt-out list is allowed only with a reason per doc (expected to be empty).
4. Citations are resolved with `pathlib` parts, never `os.sep` string joins, so the test passes on Windows.

Fake data only (Jane Q Testperson, Springfield IL). Offline: no network, no sockets (FastAPI `TestClient` is fine), no git, no installs, no new dependencies. Tests must pass on Windows CI too: `tmp_path` and `pathlib`, no hard-coded `/tmp`, no `/`-joined path strings or other POSIX-only assumptions (WO-217 broke windows-latest that way). The module under test is outside Codex's code lane: a real product bug = `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason=...)` plus a finding with file:line in VENDOR_STATUS.md; never edit it. Check `tests/`, `tests/copilot/`, `tests/codex/` and `tests/grok/` first and don't duplicate a guard. Line numbers are from main at the time of writing; re-check them in your worktree.
